title: Display Interface
concept: The Display interface provides human-readable string formatting — used by `io.println`, string interpolation, and user-facing output.
why: Without Display, your types can't be printed. Display is the default string representation for end users — friendly, readable, language-aware.
tips: Display is for end users — make it readable, localized, and pretty
Debug is for developers — make it accurate and detailed
Use string interpolation `${value}` to automatically call Display
Return FmtError on formatting failures (e.g., buffer full)
common_mistakes: Mixing Display and Debug concerns — showing internal state in Display
Forgetting that Display output might be parsed — be consistent with your format
Not implementing Display — users see Debug output instead of a friendly message
